title: Match curriculum data by content
statement: Find and match curriculum data, lesson parts and source texts by their content and structure, never by identifiers or titles, which drift or shift wholesale.
example: 224 of 239 local entries for one course matched the canonical source by content, but 218 of those sat at a different identifier.
detail: When the AP work's evaluator reconciled its history curriculum data with the canonical curriculum repository, one course's local entries turned out to be systematically off by one period: 224 of 239 had a strong content match, but 218 of those were at a different identifier (commit fb17482 in `icloud-work/inceptbench`). The merge rebuilt that course on the canonical identifiers, carried the local content onto each record by a Jaccard match, kept the old identifier on every remapped record, and carried over the 16 entries with no match unchanged.

evidence.quote: The local APEURO entries were systematically off by one period. Verified by content cross-match: 224 of 239 inceptbench APEURO entries had a strong content match in the curriculum repo, but 218 of those were at a different KC id.
- **Detection is structural, never by node id or title.**

The source is confirmed by what the lesson's reading chunks contain, not by the lesson's `lessonId`. A course file whose ids lag the folder scheme still gets checked; the mismatch is reported as info.
File names or equal counts are insufficient.
The named shared-app ZIP is the prior handoff again and contains no current-build advantage.
